name: Existing Business and Growth Option Separation

positioning.oneLineSummary: Separates existing-business value from uncertain growth opportunities and permits separate option treatment only when incremental rights and no-double-count controls pass.
positioning.productLabel: Growth-Option Separation Lens — based on Mauboussin and Rappaport's public real-options materials
notAClaimOf: a large TAM being an option
all startup upside deserving a separate premium
accounting intangibles automatically creating option value

attribution.display: Based on Michael J. Mauboussin and Alfred Rappaport's public real-options and intangible-investment materials

neutralParaphrase: Value the operating business and growth already included in explicit forecasts or residual value first. A separate growth option is eligible only when the company has a specific incremental opportunity, meaningful access or exclusivity, an identifiable exercise cost and decision window, and a reconciliation proving the same cash flows are absent from the base model.

locator.value: Value of existing business plus real options for uncertain growth opportunities and implied option gap
Intangible-investment treatment and real-options role in expectations analysis
Public report: analytical treatment of intangible investment and reconciliation of invested capital

requiredConditions: Existing-business and explicit-growth cash flows are defined first.
The proposed option is incremental and company-specific.
Access or exclusivity, exercise cost, decision trigger, option life, and erosion are identified.
A line-by-line reconciliation proves no overlap with explicit forecast, residual value, or another option.
Any intangible capitalization adjustment preserves total free cash flow.

requiredEvidence.description: Existing-business DCF and schedule of all explicit and residual growth assumptions.
Specific project, market, technology, data, patent, license, contract, or platform right that creates differentiated access.
Exercise cost, decision trigger, time window, information arrival, erosion, and abandonment conditions.
If R&D or other intangibles are capitalized analytically, a reconciliation to reported accounts and unchanged total free cash flow.

decisionQuestions: Which cash flows belong to the existing business?
Which growth paths are already in the explicit forecast or residual value?
What incremental right gives this company differentiated access to the opportunity?
What are the exercise cost, trigger, life, and erosion mechanism?
Can management wait for useful information before committing?
Does any intangible reclassification preserve free cash flow?
positiveSignals: A legally, technically, contractually, or structurally differentiated right exists.
The company can defer major investment until decision-relevant information arrives.
Exercise cost, term, trigger, and erosion are source-linked.
The opportunity's cash flows are absent from the base DCF and residual value.
Intangible adjustments reconcile without creating cash.
redFlags: The option is only a large TAM or management aspiration.
No exercise cost, decision point, or finite window exists.
The same growth appears in forecasts, terminal value, and option value.
Capitalizing expenses increases FCF without reconciliation.
disconfirmingEvidence: The right expires before technical, regulatory, or commercial readiness.
Competition can enter on equivalent terms.
Investment must be committed before useful information arrives.
The project is already required to sustain the base business.
Reasonable option inputs make incremental value immaterial or indeterminate.
contraindications: Do not call generic managerial flexibility a real option.
Do not add option value without company-specific access.
Do not let accounting reclassification create cash.
Do not let the LLM value the option.

instructions: Reconcile existing-business, explicit-growth, and residual-value cash flows.
Test incremental right, access, exercise, information, term, and erosion gates.
Reconcile intangible adjustments to unchanged free cash flow.
If all gates pass, send bounded inputs to the deterministic option service.
Otherwise classify the item as scenario upside, strategic possibility, or not applicable.

sourceReliability.low: The opportunity and rights rely only on narrative.
sourceReliability.medium: Project and access evidence exist but term or cost is approximate.
sourceReliability.high: Rights, project, cost, timing, competition, and model reconciliation are verified.

evidenceStrength.medium: Most option gates pass but one material range is broad.
evidenceStrength.high: All gates and no-double-count reconciliation pass with independent evidence.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only TAM and opportunity are covered.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Access, project, and cost are covered but erosion or reconciliation is partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Base value, access, exercise, timing, erosion, competition, and reconciliation are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: Opportunity is shared, required, or already modeled.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: It resembles an option but exclusivity or life is uncertain.
applicabilityConfidence.high: It has a clear incremental option structure.

judgmentConfidence.low: No separate option treatment is supportable.
judgmentConfidence.medium: A bounded option range may be calculated with caveats.
judgmentConfidence.high: A deterministic option calculation and reconciliation are supportable.

promotionRequirements: Validate option gates and model choices by sector.
empiricalQualifications: Project volatility, option life, and competitive erosion are difficult to estimate.
Many startup opportunities are better represented as scenarios than separate options.
Access can disappear before formal legal rights expire.

rights.notes: Official public companion materials are neutrally paraphrased and adapted through explicit product gates.
